dependencies.title: Foundation: CI executes every notebook offline and validates fixtures
dependencies.body:
## Goal

The gate every recipe pull request has to pass. Once this is merged, recipes can start.

## Scope

- A CI job that discovers every `recipes/*/notebook.ipynb`, executes it from a fresh environment with no key and `JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE` unset, and fails on any error.
- Fixture validation for every recipe folder.
- A guard that fails if a notebook attempts a network call to the TypeSafe API during the offline run.
- A check that committed notebook outputs match a fresh offline execution closely enough to catch stale outputs (define the comparison and document it).
- A check that a recipe pull request changes only its own `recipes/NN-slug/` folder, reported as a clear message.
- Per-recipe execution in a matrix or with path filtering, so sixty notebooks do not make every run slow.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The template recipe passes all jobs
- [ ] A notebook with a failing cell, an invalid fixture, and a stale output each make CI fail, demonstrated in the pull request description
- [ ] Full run time with one recipe is recorded, with a note on how it scales
- [ ] Lint and tests pass in CI, or locally with the output pasted in the pull request if CI does not exist yet

## Dependencies

- Blocked by #62 (CI baseline for lint, tests, and the README catalog check)
- Blocked by #68 (recipe template and scaffolder)
- Unblocks every recipe issue (#1 to #60)
- Tracked in #74

dependencies.body:
> Recipe **29** of 60 · Level 3 (Intermediate) · Agent orchestration · `Choice`

## Use case

Classify recorded tool outcomes as complete, partial, failed, or unverifiable using the original request and observed evidence.

## What to build

The folder `recipes/29-tool-outcome-verification/` with `notebook.ipynb`, `README.md`, and `fixtures/`, meeting the [recipe contract](https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). Start from `python tools/new_recipe.py 29` and the template in `recipes/_template/`.

### Build notes

- Outcomes: `complete`, `partial`, `failed`, `unverifiable`.
- State is the original request plus the recorded evidence from the tool run.
- Include runs that report success with no supporting evidence.

### Decision design

- **Choice.** Options are a fixed set supplied by Python, including the fallback outcome this use case names. Show the `choice`, the per-option `probabilities`, and the `confidence` for individual examples before aggregating.

### Level 3 scope

Multiple judgments or stages, structured evidence, deterministic composition, and task-level evaluation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `recipes/29-tool-outcome-verification/notebook.ipynb` runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network, and its outputs are committed
- [ ] Live mode is opt-in (`JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE=1` with `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`) and uses the same question definitions as the offline run
- [ ] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases named in the build notes, carry gold labels, and pass the fixture validator
- [ ] Every response fixture records its provenance, and the notebook states which mode it ran in
- [ ] Evaluation: Confusion matrix, with `unverifiable` discussed on its own.
- [ ] The deterministic composition lives in a Python function with tests in `tests/`
- [ ] Evaluation is at task level, not only per question
- [ ] No statement about Jev's quality, latency, or cost appears without recorded live inference; in a synthetic run, metrics are labelled as pipeline checks
- [ ] `recipes/29-tool-outcome-verification/README.md` says what the recipe teaches, how to run it, and what was and was not measured live
- [ ] The pull request changes only `recipes/29-tool-outcome-verification/` and CI is green

## Dependencies

- Blocked by #69 (CI executes every notebook offline and validates fixtures)
- Tracked in #77

## Sources

Read these before writing the questions.

- S02 · [TypeSafe AI: Primitives (Questions)](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives): Choice, Noul, Score, independent questions, and dependent follow-up calls.
- S03 · [TypeSafe AI: Confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence): Distribution-derived confidence and task-specific thresholds informed by observed outcomes.
- S04 · [TypeSafe AI: How to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one): Narrow semantic judgments integrated with workflows, deterministic logic, and side effects controlled by code.
- S06 · [TypeSafe AI: Cookbooks](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks): Worked patterns for extraction, citation checking, skill selection, hierarchical classification, and feature discovery.

## Out of scope

- Changes to shared code, the catalog, or the root README. If the shared package is missing something, open a foundation issue and link it here.
- Real side effects of any kind. Actions are simulated.

dependencies.title: evaluation: noul_confidence must be |2p − 1| per the confidence page (same scale as Choice); document the Noul three-path pattern
dependencies.body:
## Context

From the Opus review of #136 (recipe 02, the first Noul recipe; comment 6071121590). `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py` and `docs/evaluation.md` define `noul_confidence(p) = max(p, 1 − p)` (range 0.5–1). The TypeSafe confidence page (`https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence.md`, README S03) defines a Noul's confidence as `|2p − 1|` (range 0–1) and states it is the Choice formula `(p_max − 1/n)/(1 − 1/n)` applied with n = 2, so it sits on the same scale as Choice confidence. The toolkit helper therefore disagrees with the source, and a recipe that gates Nouls and Choices with one threshold, as the page recommends, gets wrong answers from it. `docs/evaluation.md` documents the Choice rescaling correctly on the same page.

## Acceptance

1. `noul_confidence(p)` returns `|2p − 1|` per the confidence page (the old `max(p, 1 − p)` is removed or kept under a distinct, documented name such as `noul_majority`); `docs/evaluation.md` and `docs/glossary.md` state the formula with the source link and note the shared scale with Choice.
2. Tests pin the formula at p ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1} and the identity with `(p_max − 1/n)/(1 − 1/n)` at n = 2; mutation: revert to `max(p, 1 − p)` → tests fail.
3. Every call site in `src/`, `recipes/_template`, `tools/new_recipe.py` and merged recipes is checked; any notebook whose outputs change is re-executed and committed byte-identically in the same PR (list them).
4. Add to `docs/evaluation.md` a short "Noul three-path pattern" note: a business threshold on p plus a confidence gate `|2p − 1| < c` → review outcome, composed from `threshold_sweep` / `evaluate_threshold`, since no helper selects both together (the Score recipes reported the same gap).

Required before the remaining Noul recipes (#6, #10, and later waves) are briefed. Foundation issue; allowed paths `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py`, `tests/test_evaluation*.py`, `docs/evaluation.md`, `docs/glossary.md`, plus re-executed notebooks only if their outputs change.

dependencies.title: Foundation: opt-in live Jev backend and response recorder
dependencies.body:
## Goal

Let a reader with their own key run any recipe against Jev, and capture those responses as recorded fixtures.

## Scope

- `LiveBackend` wrapping `typesafe_sdk.TypeSafeClient.system_one`, available only with the `live` extra, `JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE=1`, and `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`.
- The model is passed explicitly per run. The `model` string the API returns and the `usage` block are kept on the result.
- A request budget guard: a maximum number of calls per run, enforced in code, with a clear error when exceeded.
- A recorder that writes responses into a recipe's fixtures with provenance `recorded`, the returned model string, and the date.
- A documented path for alternative backends through the System One Adapter (S08), needed by recipes 50 and 55. Decide whether that is an optional extra and write the decision down.
- The key never appears in logs, exceptions, fixtures, or notebook output.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests run with the HTTP layer mocked; CI makes no network call and needs no key
- [ ] Missing key or missing opt-in gives a clear, actionable error
- [ ] A test shows the budget guard stops a run
- [ ] A test shows recorded fixtures replay through `ReplayBackend` byte for byte
- [ ] The pull request states whether a real live call was made during development. If none was, it says so

dependencies.title: evaluation: noul_confidence must be |2p − 1| per the confidence page (same scale as Choice); document the Noul three-path pattern
dependencies.body:
## Context

From the Opus review of #136 (recipe 02, the first Noul recipe; comment 6071121590). `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py` and `docs/evaluation.md` define `noul_confidence(p) = max(p, 1 − p)` (range 0.5–1). The TypeSafe confidence page (`https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence.md`, README S03) defines a Noul's confidence as `|2p − 1|` (range 0–1) and states it is the Choice formula `(p_max − 1/n)/(1 − 1/n)` applied with n = 2, so it sits on the same scale as Choice confidence. The toolkit helper therefore disagrees with the source, and a recipe that gates Nouls and Choices with one threshold, as the page recommends, gets wrong answers from it. `docs/evaluation.md` documents the Choice rescaling correctly on the same page.

## Acceptance

1. `noul_confidence(p)` returns `|2p − 1|` per the confidence page (the old `max(p, 1 − p)` is removed or kept under a distinct, documented name such as `noul_majority`); `docs/evaluation.md` and `docs/glossary.md` state the formula with the source link and note the shared scale with Choice.
2. Tests pin the formula at p ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1} and the identity with `(p_max − 1/n)/(1 − 1/n)` at n = 2; mutation: revert to `max(p, 1 − p)` → tests fail.
3. Every call site in `src/`, `recipes/_template`, `tools/new_recipe.py` and merged recipes is checked; any notebook whose outputs change is re-executed and committed byte-identically in the same PR (list them).
4. Add to `docs/evaluation.md` a short "Noul three-path pattern" note: a business threshold on p plus a confidence gate `|2p − 1| < c` → review outcome, composed from `threshold_sweep` / `evaluate_threshold`, since no helper selects both together (the Score recipes reported the same gap).

Required before the remaining Noul recipes (#6, #10, and later waves) are briefed. Foundation issue; allowed paths `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py`, `tests/test_evaluation*.py`, `docs/evaluation.md`, `docs/glossary.md`, plus re-executed notebooks only if their outputs change.
